criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use an elevated oblique projection with diagonal ground axes.
Both maintain a broadly consistent yaw and pitch across their ROI sequences.
different: REFERENCE frames closer, terrain-led compositions with stronger vertical relief.
CANDIDATE is more top-down and exposes a wider rectilinear road-and-tile layout.

evidence.observation: R01 shows a close oblique view with rugged relief and an organically framed river valley.
R01 uses a similar isometric direction but reveals more planar roads, lots, and grid-aligned ground.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both depict a winding river embedded in rocky industrial terrain.
Both show a metal road bridge attached to opposite banks during the sequence.
different: REFERENCE water is a broad reflective channel with deep, softly modeled banks.
CANDIDATE begins as a narrow graphic-blue ribbon, then expands into sharply bounded flood coverage with limited reflection.

evidence.observation: R02 contains a broad sinuous channel with shaded bank depth and muted surface reflection.
R02 contains a narrower, darker-blue channel bounded by crisp layered contours.
R06 shows an industrial bridge seated across the channel and connected to dense riverside facilities.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use dark industrial metal, brown-black soil, and restrained amber lighting.
Both combine rocky terrain with steel bridges, towers, and factory structures.
different: REFERENCE has richer surface grain, atmospheric midtones, water reflections, and softer material transitions.
CANDIDATE is flatter and more outline-heavy, with dark tiled concrete and sharper graphic overlays.

evidence.observation: R06 shows textured blackened structures, fine rocky soil, warm bridge lights, and subdued reflective water.
R06 shows the same industrial palette but with flatter road slabs, harder contours, and sprite-like material separation.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both sequences move from a dark normal river setting toward strongly amber and cyan-accented conditions.
CANDIDATE preserves recognizable roads, buildings, bridge, and pylons across its normal, heat, and flood views.
different: REFERENCE conveys stressed terrain through localized cracked soil and integrated lighting rather than broad color masks.
CANDIDATE heat is dominated by a uniform amber wash, while flood becomes a large graphic-blue fill with bright contour borders.

evidence.observation: R09 presents a dry cracked terrain state with localized warm highlights and an energized cyan route.
R09 retains the base-world roads and buildings beneath a broad translucent amber heat treatment.
R11 retains industrial landmarks while blue floodwater and bright cyan boundaries cover much of the ground.
